item.title: Pay Solar Installers When STC or Finance Money Is Late
item.description:
The job’s done. The panels are on the roof, the inverter’s commissioned and your installer has sent their invoice. But the STC money hasn’t come through. The finance provider hasn’t settled either, and the customer’s balance is stuck behind both of them. Your subbie still has a mortgage, a ute payment and a crew to pay on Thursday.

Search for help with this and nearly everything you find is written for the subcontractor chasing money: lien rights, demand letters, US construction stats. Very little is written for the person in the middle, the solar business owner who wants to pay their installers properly but is waiting on money that hasn’t landed yet.

item.title: STCs Aren't a Rebate: How Australia's Solar Certificate Scheme Actually Works
item.description:
I have lost count of how many times I have heard an installer, a salesperson, and a customer all sit at the same kitchen table calling the same thing a “rebate”. The system price drops by a few thousand dollars, everyone nods, and the job gets signed. Nobody in the room actually knows what just happened.

That is fine for the customer. It is not fine for you, the operator. Because the thing you keep calling a rebate is a tradeable financial certificate with a price that moves, paperwork that has to be lodged correctly, and a settlement timeline that can quietly strangle your working capital if you treat it like free government money landing in your account.
